status: source-layer sensitivity lane; not manuscript-secure primary calibration

dateClasses.D1: source layer is strongly argued to predate outcome; surviving witness is later
dateClasses.D4: date is materially inferred from apparent fulfilment

codingRule.warning: Outcome values are annotation targets for sensitivity analysis, not measurements. Every case retains its component-level dispute.

cases.targetBreadth: broad geopolitical defeat, kingship loss and exile
cases.annotation: Eighth-century northern material plausibly predates Assyrian annexation, but the final book is layered and the imagery does not define one narrow event predicate.

rivals.claim: An eighth-century northern warning substantially anticipates Assyrian defeat and exile.
rivals.scoringEffect: permits partial predictive credit

rivals.claim: The extant formulation includes exilic or post-event shaping.
rivals.scoringEffect: removes independent predictive credit from the final form

rivals.claim: The imagery is broad judgment rhetoric rather than one narrowly testable event forecast.
rivals.scoringEffect: reduces specificity even if pre-event

cases.targetBreadth: defeat, plunder and exile of the northern kingdom
cases.annotation: Traditional source placement predates Samaria's fall, while substantial scholarship allows post-722 literary-predictive shaping; the case is therefore dating-sensitive.

rivals.claim: A pre-722 Amos core forecasts defeat, plunder and exile.
rivals.scoringEffect: permits partial predictive credit

rivals.claim: The literary prediction was materially shaped after Samaria fell.
rivals.scoringEffect: treats the fit as retrospective

rivals.claim: Imperial defeat was a live political risk and the target remains broad.
rivals.scoringEffect: discounts surprise and specificity

cases.targetBreadth: failure of the Syro-Ephraimite coalition and removal of its two kings, with a disputed sixty-five-year gloss
cases.annotation: The near-term coalition outcome fits the eighth-century crisis; the sixty-five-year clause, textual layering and later Immanuel reception must not be scored as one undifferentiated prediction.

rivals.claim: The sign concerns the immediate Syro-Ephraimite crisis and its two kings.
rivals.scoringEffect: scores only the near-term geopolitical components

rivals.claim: The sixty-five-year clause belongs to a distinct or later textual layer.
rivals.scoringEffect: forbids combining all clauses into one successful horizon

rivals.claim: Christian Immanuel interpretation is a later typological horizon.
rivals.scoringEffect: records reception separately from the eighth-century outcome

cases.annotation: The target matches Nineveh's fall, but scholarly models place relevant composition before, during or after the event; the case cannot carry one fixed pre-event weight.

rivals.claim: The relevant oracle predates Nineveh's fall.
rivals.scoringEffect: permits predictive credit subject to specificity

rivals.claim: The text arose during the terminal campaign or siege.
rivals.scoringEffect: reduces lead time and surprise

rivals.claim: The relevant form celebrates an event already known.
rivals.scoringEffect: removes predictive credit

cases.annotation: Candidate intervals such as 609-539 and 587-517 illustrate genuine near-seventy correspondences, but domination, destruction, return and temple restoration are different endpoints.

rivals.claim: The seventy years span Babylonian regional domination.
rivals.scoringEffect: yields an approximately seventy-year interval

rivals.claim: The interval runs from Jerusalem's destruction to restored temple worship.
rivals.scoringEffect: yields a rival approximately seventy-year interval

rivals.claim: Seventy is a conventional fullness or lifetime number rather than exact arithmetic.
rivals.scoringEffect: disallows exact endpoint optimisation

cases.targetBreadth: Nebuchadnezzar obtains decisive destruction and spoil from Tyre
cases.annotation: The later dated oracle acknowledges no wages from Tyre and redirects compensation to Egypt. Later Alexander fulfilment readings change the named-agent predicate and are logged as repairs.

rivals.claim: Nebuchadnezzar is the named agent expected to obtain Tyre's spoil.
rivals.scoringEffect: scores the declared predicate as a miss

rivals.claim: The oracle concerns successive nations culminating in later destruction.
rivals.scoringEffect: broadens agent and horizon and must pay a repair penalty

rivals.claim: Ezekiel 29 redirects wages to Egypt after the Tyre outcome.
rivals.scoringEffect: records an internal update rather than retroactive success

cases.targetBreadth: detailed Seleucid sequence followed by Antiochus IV's final campaign and death
cases.annotation: The sequence closely tracks events before diverging at the terminal campaign and death. That transition is used to date the source, so it cannot independently validate foresight.

rivals.claim: The sequence is retrospective until its inaccurate Antiochus endpoint.
rivals.scoringEffect: uses the case as an ex-eventu control, not predictive validation

rivals.claim: An earlier source genuinely anticipates the Seleucid sequence in approximate form.
rivals.scoringEffect: would permit predictive credit only with independent source dating

rivals.claim: The terminal verses project beyond Antiochus to a later eschatological antagonist.
rivals.scoringEffect: changes the historical target and remains open rather than rescuing the Antiochus endpoint
